head: WhatsApp scams: fake Black Friday deals spread through friends' chats
dek: Security firm KnowBe4 Africa warns South Africans that the riskiest Black Friday links on WhatsApp come from people they know, sent from taken-over accounts or forwarded in good faith.
details: Criminals take over a contact's WhatsApp through a SIM swap or by tricking them into sharing their verification code, according to KnowBe4 Africa's Anna Collard. Last November, Africa Check found a fake Shoprite Black Friday sale link going around WhatsApp and Facebook groups; it was a phishing page that asked for phone numbers and email addresses, and Shoprite distanced itself from it. KnowBe4 Africa's research found 89% of South African respondents use WhatsApp for work, so a taken-over phone can also expose work email and authenticator apps.
where: South Africa, Black Friday 2026; WhatsApp on any phone
means: If a friend or colleague sends you a Black Friday deal on WhatsApp, the link can still be fake, even when the message really comes from their account.
todo: Buy only through the shop's own app or website. Check an unknown seller's reviews and how new its website is. Don't enter a login or card details for a voucher. If a link looks wrong, call the sender to check. Turn on two-step verification in WhatsApp under Settings, Account, Two-step verification.
